chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Luck of recording and the lack of names on records
summary: Whether you got on a record was luck, and early records did not list the sidemen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I guess some times it's a matter of luck too. At least it was in those days, if you happened to be with a band that got to record, and the records were unlabeled but they would get around a little bit.
That would make a little difference.
Yeah. But these days -- I don't think
they put the names of guys on records no more do they. Not much.
Well, they put it on the folder, but when you get to the record -- suppose the folder gets lost. You got a record you don't know who played what. You know.
Yeah. Well by now they've got others -- discographies and everything.
Yeah. Well you know several guys had to pay some more money --
It took a long time. It took a long time to find out who played on all those (inaudible).
I know it. I know it. Because they didn't put no names -- you know -- just the guy that made a record.
